From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Amanda Jones <amanda.jones@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Phased push: readiness checklist, doc owners, and exception requests

Team —

We are targeting a phased push for the Acme Health integration the week of Jan 4. Before we lock the window I want to align on the minimum readiness bar and capture any required exceptions. High level ask: can each of you confirm owners and ETA for the items below by EOD Monday?

Must-haves (minimum for phase 1):
- API contract parity doc reviewed and signed off
- Enablement playbook (CS runbook + customer-facing notes)
- Rollout canary parameters and monitoring thresholds
- Security checklist sign-off (SOC evidence already requested separately)

Proposed owners:
- Product / API: Marissa
- Docs & Enablement: Laura
- Rollout & Ops: Ben
- Account escalation / executive comms: Vivek

I've attached a short phased_push_proposal.pdf with the proposed stages and fallback policies. Also cc'ing Amanda from Acme so they're aware we'll be coordinating timings — Amanda you can ignore unless you have questions.

Rishi
Director, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: phased_push_proposal.pdf (PDF, 235KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Amanda Jones <amanda.jones@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Phased push: readiness checklist, doc owners, and exception requests

Thanks Rishi — quick product update and a couple of asks.

1) API freeze window: Engineering can commit to a freeze for endpoint shape changes from Dec 28–Jan 3, but we need an explicit exception for a small opt-in header change that the analytics team requires (it does not change payload schema, only header semantics). This would be backwards-compatible but needs a canary on production traffic to validate.

2) Feature gating: To minimize blast radius we'll gate the new model routing behind a customer flag for Acme only in phase 1. That needs a short engineering task and a rollback plan (estimated 2–3 dev days).

3) Docs: I'll partner with Laura on the API contract doc and will add acceptance tests to the PR.

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa to open SUP-9876 for the header opt-in exception (engineering + QA runbook)
- Laura to own enablement checklist completion and CS runbook
- Ben to confirm monitoring dashboards and canary thresholds

Onward —
Marissa
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

All — I've reviewed the proposal and can confirm we can run a 5% canary for the first 48 hours and expand to 20% on day 3, subject to these thresholds:

- Error rate < 0.5% sustained over 30m
- P95 latency < 280ms
- Retries triggered -> auto-fallback to stable model variant

I'll create a small monitoring dashboard and the incident runbook. Attaching a tiny text file with the canary parameters we will commit to.

One ask: if Marissa's header opt-in exception is required, it must go through SUP-9876 with an explicit QA checklist (noted).

Ben
Director, Production Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: canary_parameters.txt (TXT, 2KB)

- Marissa: open SUP-9876 for header opt-in exception + acceptance tests (ETA: Dec 17)
- Laura: publish internal runbook (ETA: Dec 22) and customer page (ETA: Dec 29); schedule CS enablement (proposed Dec 30)
- Ben: monitoring dashboard + incident runbook, implement canary thresholds (ETA: Dec 21)

If we hit these milestones we can start the phased push the week of Jan 4. If anything blocks, flag it in this thread and I'll escalate.
